### Issue description

When importing a glb file with an animation, if "Save to File" is enabled and "Keep Custom Tracks" is on, while markers are saved to the file when you create them, if you reimport the glb file, the markers are deleted from the file.

title: Changing length of animation in a named AnimationLibrary doesn't update current_animation_length
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2, and in my current compiled 4.8 branch
- this is regression from 4.6, where this bug didn't happen.

### System information

Godot v4.6.3.stable (35e80b3a8) - cpe:/o:nixos:nixos:26.11 26.11 (Zokor) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Graphics (ADL GT2) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1240P (16 threads) - 15.33 GiB memory

### Issue description

If you add an Animation to an AnimationLibrary and set it playing and you dynamically change the animation's length the update doesn't get respected in the AnimationPlayer, so when you try to seek to time points outside of its cached value it clamps it to the wrong animation length.

(I'm using the feature of inserting keys into a running animation to interpolate the keyframe positions of a remote player over the network.)

### Steps to reproduce

The following prints the animation length set to 10, but the AnimationPlayer 

```GDScript
func _ready():
	var animation := Animation.new()
	animation.length = 1.0

	var track := animation.add_track(Animation.TYPE_POSITION_3D)
	animation.track_set_path(track, ^"Target")
	animation.track_insert_key(track, 0.0, Vector3.ZERO)

	var library := AnimationLibrary.new()
	library.add_animation(&"test", animation)
	$AnimationPlayer.add_animation_library(&"playeral", library)
	$AnimationPlayer.play(&"playeral/test")
	$AnimationPlayer.pause()

	# Extend the already assigned animation.
	animation.length = 10.0
	animation.track_insert_key(track, 5.0, Vector3(99, 0, 0))

	var seek_time = 5.0
	print("Seeking to ", seek_time)
	$AnimationPlayer.seek(seek_time, true)

	print("Resource length: ", animation.length)
	print("Player length:   ", $AnimationPlayer.current_animation_length)
	print("Seek position:   ", $AnimationPlayer.current_animation_position)
```

In 4.7 and 4.8 this prints:

```
Seeking to 5.0
Resource length: 10.0
Player length:   1.0
Seek position:   1.0
```

In 4.6 this prints:

```
Seeking to 5.0
Resource length: 10.0
Player length:   10.0
Seek position:   5.0
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[animation_bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33555303/animation_bug.zip)

The suspect is the `AnimationLibrary.animation_changed` signal not using the full path of the animation.

title: macOS export with Shader Baker crashes on start: “Not enough bytes for uniform in shader container” (Metal, 4.7.2)
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.7.0.stable and 4.7.2.stable (official builds)

### System information

macOS 26 (Tahoe), Apple M2 Pro, Metal 4.0 – Forward+, Xcode installed (metal/metallib toolchain available)

### Issue description

A macOS export with Shader Baker enabled crashes on start as soon as user://shader_cache is empty (fresh install). The log shows for ~21 shaders, including engine shaders such as VolumetricFogShaderRD and SceneForwardClusteredShaderRD:

ERROR: Not enough bytes for uniform in shader container.
   at: from_bytes (servers/rendering/rendering_shader_container.cpp:818)
ERROR: Failed to parse shader container from binary.
   at: shader_create_from_bytecode_with_samplers (servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:4179)
ERROR: Condition "shader.is_null()" is true. Returning: false
   at: _load_from_cache (servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shader_rd.cpp:679)
ERROR: Parameter "shader" is null.
ERROR: FATAL: Index p_index = 35 is out of bounds (size() = 0).
handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 5

Same result with application/min_macos_version_arm64 = 11.00 and 15.00.
The export log contains no “requires Apple… but target is…” warnings, so no shader was marked invalid during baking.
Without Shader Baker the export works. But the first start compiles shaders for ~3.5 minutes (blocked/white screen), which is what the baker is meant to avoid.
Side effect: after the crash, the baked containers are copied to user://shader_cache, and even a later export without baker crashes until that folder is deleted.
Possibly related observation while reading the source (drivers/metal/rendering_shader_container_metal.cpp, also on master): when a shader is mark_invalid()-ed during baking, _to_bytes_reflection_binding_uniform_extra_data() and _to_bytes_shader_extra_data() write 0 bytes, but _from_bytes_reflection_binding_uniform_extra_data() / _from_bytes_shader_extra_data() always read sizeof(UniformData) / sizeof(StageData). That would produce exactly this error for invalid shaders. In our case no shader seems to be marked invalid, so there may be a second cause.

### Steps to reproduce

Forward+ project with a few 3D materials, volumetric fog / environment effects, MetalFX Temporal upscaling.
macOS export preset, Shader Baker enabled, export from the editor (not headless) to .dmg/.app.
Delete ~/Library/Application Support/Godot/app_userdata/<project>/shader_cache and the app’s Metal cache ($(getconf DARWIN_USER_CACHE_DIR)<bundle id>).

title: String.to_float() does not correctly round; reads DBL_MIN and subnormals as 0
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.8.dev [4d10419ca], 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf]
   - on both Linux x86_64 Ubuntu 24.04 and macOS arm64
- `core/string/ustring.cpp` is basically unchanged since v1.0, so I doubt this is a regression.

### System information

macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 - Godot v4.7.2.stable.mono.official [ed1daf0bf]

### Issue description

Ran into this rounding issue when porting a game from C# to GDScript/C++ 
 
- String.to_float() does not return the nearest double; reads values below about 1e-292 as 0.
- Since #98750 and #108836 Godot writes doubles with Grisu2, so the text comes back under a correcty rounded parser, but Godot fails read back:
    - `JSON.stringify(x, "", true, true)` documents that it writes digits "to guarantee exact decoding", yet `JSON.parse_string()` returns a different double for values in practice.
    - GDScript literals with more than about 15 significant digits can compile to a neighboring double (1.44269504088896338700 is one ULP off), and 2.2250738585072014e-308 (DBL_MIN) compiles to 0.0.

- **Related issue** #123700 mentions the rounding and "1e-320" → 0 only as a "related, lower priority" note under a different bug (leading zeros), and its fix #123839 says the rounding is out of scope. Filing separately so they don't close together.
    - Both come from the same root; a correctly rounded parser fixes both, and #123700 too.

**Partial Fix**
This stop gap solution (below) prevents ~1e-292 reading as 0; the rounding needs a correctly rounded, e.g. [fast_float](https://github.com/fastfloat/fast_float).

```diff
--- a/core/string/ustring.cpp
+++ b/core/string/ustring.cpp
@@ -2555,6 +2555,12 @@ static double built_in_strtod(
 		exp = maxExponent;
 		WARN_PRINT("Exponent too high");
 	}
+	// 10^exp overflows a double past 10^308, and dividing by infinity would turn values as large as
+	// 2.2250738585072014e-308 (DBL_MIN) into 0. Divide by 10^256 first so the rest stays finite.

title: Compute shader with barrier throws error when replaying push constants onto a shader that uses none
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: Godot v4.7, Godot v4.8 (current master)

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable.mono - macOS Sequoia (15.6.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M3 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M3 Pro (12 threads) - 18.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

### Short Description:
If a compute list sets push constants for one shader, then binds a shader that uses none, `compute_list_add_barrier()` replays the previous shader's push constants. A dev build then reports a size error.
The check returns before those bytes are recorded, so the dispatch is not given them. A barrier that stays on the same pipeline still restores that pipeline's constants.

### Steps to reproduce: 
1. Begin a compute list
2. Bind compute pipeline A with shader that using push constants. Call `compute_list_set_push_constant` and dispatch.
3. Bind compute pipeline B with a shader that not using push constants. Do not call  `compute_list_set_push_constant `.
4. Add barrier for pipeline B while it's still bound.

Editor will show following error:
```
This compute pipeline requires (0) bytes of push constant data, supplied: (4) <C++ Error> Condition "p_data_size != compute_list.validation.pipeline_push_constant_size" is true. <C++ Source> servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp @ compute_list_set_push_constant()
```

### Why this happens:
`compute_list_add_barrier()` replays push constants stored on compute list. Binding a new pipeline does not clear stored push constants size, so barrier calls compute_list_set_push_constant with old shader push constants data and size.

### Workaround:
You can explicitly call `compute_list_set_push_constant` after every pipeline bind, including shaders without push constants (just pass zero size), that way compute list will always have actual push constants state and barrier will not break.

You can use MRP attached to the issue

### Issue description

The editor crashes on exit when a GDExtension has registered an OpenXR extension wrapper through the deprecated `OpenXRExtensionWrapperExtension` class. An empty project with the Godot OpenXR Vendors add-on (any release up to 4.3.1) is enough; no XR setting needs to be enabled. Expected: clean exit, as in 4.7.2 and 4.8.dev1.

#121417 changed `OpenXRAPI::cleanup_extension_wrappers()` from

		if (gdextension_extension_wrapper) {

		} else
#endif
		{

		}
```

to

```cpp
		memdelete(gdextension_extension_wrapper);
#endif
		memdelete(extension_wrapper);
```

When the `dynamic_cast` succeeds, both `memdelete` calls now run on the same object, so it is freed twice and the second call crashes in `Object::_predelete()`. The null check added in #121416 does not help here, since the second pointer is dangling rather than null.

The if/else came from #88689, the fix for #88613 (same crash, same add-on). Since #104087 the deprecated class is a plain subclass of `OpenXRExtensionWrapper`, so both pointers are the same address and the `dynamic_cast` no longer serves a purpose.

Reverting the `cleanup_extension_wrappers` hunk of #121417 fixes it: with a local build of master at 12c17c187 the editor crashes on exit as above, and with the hunk reverted it exits cleanly. Deleting the whole `#ifndef DISABLE_DEPRECATED` block and keeping a single `memdelete(extension_wrapper)` also fixes it. Happy to open a PR for whichever form is preferred.

The Vendors plugin stopped using the deprecated class in 5.0.0 (GodotVR/godot_openxr_vendors#414), so 5.x releases are not affected. Older releases and any third-party GDExtension still on `OpenXRExtensionWrapperExtension` are.

### System information

### Issue description

The project below does nothing except log frame intervals from one Node2D. It still drops one long frame, 24–40 ms at 120 Hz, **~15.07 s after engine start, in every launch**:
- The instant is the same within ±40 ms on the standard and .NET builds, on both drivers.
- In a game it lands mid-play as a visible hitch.

**Where the frame goes.** I timestamped the first and last `_process`, `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` / `frame_post_draw`, and an `InputEventAction` injected each frame and seen in `_input` at the next event flush.
- The whole stall falls **after `frame_post_draw` and before the next input flush**. That is between iterations, in the AppKit run loop, not in scripts, physics or rendering.
- On that frame the viewport's CPU render time is ~0.1 ms.

**What runs there.** The unified log shows, at the same instant, on the **main thread**:

```
21:26:23.263 Godot[64184:db00db] [com.apple.AppKit:StateRestoration] -[NSPersistentUIManager flushAllChanges]
21:26:23.263 Godot[64184:db00db] [com.apple.AppKit:StateRestoration] -[NSPersistentUIManager flushAllChanges] Emptying for initial flush.
21:26:23.291 Godot[64184:db00db] [com.apple.AppKit:StateRestoration] -[NSPersistentUIManager flushAllChanges] finishing enqueued operations

title: `SceneTree` accessibility change queue grows forever without screen reader support (headless / no AccessKit)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.5-stable and later (tested 4.6.3-stable, 4.7.2-stable), current `master` (4.8-dev) has the same code.
- Not reproducible in: 4.4.1-stable (no accessibility API yet).

All builds are from source without the AccessKit dependencies (the build prints "The screen reader support driver requires dependencies to be installed").

### System information

Arch Linux (kernel 7.2.9), AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 8840HS. Reproduced with `--headless` and with the X11 display server; our target is Linux.

### Issue description

`SceneTree::accessibility_change_queue` (`HashSet<ObjectID>`) grows forever when the display server has no screen reader support (headless, or any build without AccessKit). Every GUI node that has ever been in the tree keeps its id in the set, including nodes that were freed long ago. Object count stays flat, only static memory grows.

Why:

- `Node::queue_accessibility_update()` inserts the node id unconditionally. `Control` calls it on entering the tree and on size changes, and so do `Label`, `Button`, containers and other GUI classes.
- The queue is consumed only by `_flush_accessibility_changes()` -> `_process_accessibility_changes()`, which runs only when `is_accessibility_enabled()` is true.
- On `NOTIFICATION_EXIT_TREE` the id is erased only when `is_accessibility_supported()` is true (`scene/main/node.cpp`).

Without screen reader support neither path runs, so nothing is ever removed.

The code was added in b106dfd4f9 "Base accessibility API." (#76829) and is unchanged on `master`.

Impact: in our UI-heavy app every scene change adds about 20–35 KB, and screens that create GUI nodes at runtime add more on top. An application that runs for weeks without a restart and changes scenes regularly keeps growing.

Possible fix: skip the insert in `SceneTree::_accessibility_notify_change()` when `!is_accessibility_supported()` (nothing will ever process those entries), or do the same check in `Node::queue_accessibility_update()`.

```diff
--- a/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp
+++ b/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp
@@ -243,7 +243,7 @@ void SceneTree::_accessibility_notify_change(const Node *p_node, bool p_remove)
 	if (p_node) {
 		if (p_remove) {
 			accessibility_change_queue.erase(p_node->get_instance_id());
-		} else {
+		} else if (is_accessibility_supported()) {
 			accessibility_change_queue.insert(p_node->get_instance_id());
 		}
 	}
```

title: Resources not removed from ResourceCache when using `set_path_cache`, causing use-after-free
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: current master, 4.7.2

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.4.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 Max (Apple9) - Apple M4 Max (16 threads) - 64.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Resources are not removed from the cache if the resource has `set_path_cache()` called on it before it's freed.

In the Resource destructor, if the current path isn't what it was originally set with in `set_path()`, the resource cache lookup fails.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/befe24c83135da887e534504874d1dcea4ed1f1c/core/io/resource.cpp#L790-L802

This can lead to a use-after-free if the resource is loaded again after it's been freed. If the memory allocated for the resource has been reused in the time between loads, this can cause segfaults.

While there are checks in `ResourceCache::get_ref()` for freed resources, the checks are both insufficient and dangerous; we're dereferencing something that we _know_ has been freed:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/befe24c83135da887e534504874d1dcea4ed1f1c/core/io/resource.cpp#L852-L871

title: Metal: RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED underflows when textures are freed
body:
### Tested versions

Tested versions: reproducible in 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf] and in master [c9730f40a] built locally. Not reproducible with --rendering-driver vulkan (MoltenVK) on the same machine.

### System information

macOS 26 (Darwin 25.3), Apple M4, Metal 4.0, Forward+.

### Issue description

The following is my (mostly Claude's) understanding of the issue.

Our stream's OpenTelemetry gauge for Performance.RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED read about 9.2e18. That's int() clamping the float the monitor returns, which is about 1.8e19, i.e. the uint64 counter wrapped below zero. A bare project with no game code reproduces it.

- Root cause:
  - RenderingDevice adds texture_get_allocation_size() to its counter only for textures it allocates (in texture_create and shared fallbacks). On free, it subtracts that size for every texture (_free_pending_resources).
  - Every 2D texture also gets an sRGB view (rd_texture_srgb, created by texture_create_shared in texture_storage.cpp).
  - Vulkan returns 0 for a view because it empties the view's allocation.
  - Metal returns the view's MTLTexture.allocatedSize, which is the parent's size, so each texture is subtracted twice.
  - Textures imported with texture_create_from_extension have the same asymmetry: never added, but subtracted on Metal.
- Fix: in drivers/metal/rendering_device_driver_metal.cpp, texture_get_allocation_size returns 0 for views (parentTexture() != nullptr) and for imported textures, as Vulkan does. It's 2 lines.
- Side effect: with the fix, the counter's starting value is higher (about 4.8 MB vs 2.67 MB), because views freed during startup no longer get subtracted. The new number is the accurate one.
- Not tested: the imported-texture case. It needs a GDExtension or XR texture

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached project on macOS with Godot 4.7.2 or master, using the Metal driver (the project sets rendering_device/driver.macos="metal", Forward+).
2. Run it. It waits 10 frames, creates 20 RGBA8 256×256 ImageTextures (5,242,880 bytes in all), frees them 10 frames later, prints Performance.RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED at each step, then quits. A helper in the script prints a wrapped counter as a negative number, so the drop is easy to read.
3. Look at the output. Creating adds about 5,242,880 bytes, but freeing takes off about 10,485,000, roughly twice that. The counter ends up below where it started and wraps around (it reads as about 1.8e19 without the helper).

body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable.mono.official [ed1daf0bf]

### System information

Windows 10 - `--headless` (dummy renderer). Not reproducible with Vulkan Forward+ on an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT.

### Issue description

If a `canvas_item` shader passes the built-in `TEXTURE` to one of its own functions, loading it in a headless run prints this error:

```
ERROR: Condition "!actions.custom_samplers.has(function->arguments[j].tex_builtin)" is true. Continuing.
   at: _dump_node_code (servers/rendering/shader_compiler.cpp:1329)
```

The same shader compiles without errors with a normal rendering driver. The shader is valid, and passing `TEXTURE` as an argument is the only way to use it inside a function, since functions can't access `TEXTURE` directly.

It looks like the dummy renderer's `MaterialStorage` sets up its shader compiler with empty `DefaultIdentifierActions`, so `custom_samplers` has no entry for `TEXTURE`. The RD canvas renderer sets `actions.custom_samplers["TEXTURE"] = "texture_sampler"`. The dummy renderer only compiles shaders to read their uniforms, so this is just log noise. It still shows up in every headless run, like unit tests and CI.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a project with this shader as `passed.gdshader`:

   ```glsl
   shader_type canvas_item;

   float alpha_at(sampler2D tex, vec2 t) {
       return texelFetch(tex, ivec2(t), 0).a;
   }

   void fragment() {
       COLOR = vec4(alpha_at(TEXTURE, UV * 32.0));
   }
   ```

2. Add this script as `check.gd`:

   ```gdscript
   extends SceneTree

   func _init():
       var material := ShaderMaterial.new()
       material.shader = load("res://passed.gdshader")
       quit()
   ```

3. Run `godot --headless --path . -s check.gd`.

The error above is printed. Running `godot --path . -s check.gd` without `--headless` prints nothing.

Googlebook OS - Godot v4.4 - Vulkan (Mobile) - Googlebook Laptop with Trackpad and Touchscreen

### Issue description

When using the Godot Android editor on a Googlebook laptop or tablet with a touchpad, performing a standard **two-finger scroll gesture** is interpreted by Godot as a **primary click-and-drag** (`InputEventMouseButton(BUTTON_LEFT)` followed by `InputEventMouseMotion` with `button_mask = BUTTON_MASK_LEFT`).

#### Observed Symptoms
1. **Menu items, Tree nodes, and ItemLists**: Attempting to scroll vertically through items or options reorders or drags the items instead of scrolling the container.
2. **TextEdit / CodeEdit**: Attempting to scroll through script code selects large regions of text instead of scrolling the editor view.
3. **Inspector / FileSystem docks**: Scrolling drags resources or items into other slots instead of scrolling through the property list.

#### Tested Configurations & Empirical Verification
1. **Setting: `Enable Pan and Scale Gestures` = `Off`**:
   - Result: Two-finger scroll on trackpad and touchscreen triggers click-and-drag (reordering items, selecting text).
2. **Setting: `Enable Pan and Scale Gestures` = `On` (restarted editor)**:
   - Result: Still reproducible. Exactly the same click-and-drag behavior occurs when two-finger scrolling.
3. **Screencast Demonstration**:
   - Video recording: https://youtu.be/Fm-lgbizPoM demonstrating two-finger scroll attempts resulting in click-and-drag in the editor.

1. `onDown` in `GodotGestureHandler.kt` immediately emits touch down which is converted to an emulated `InputEventMouseButton (LEFT, pressed=true)` because `emulate_mouse_from_touch = true` is enforced in the editor (`main.cpp`).

3. Controls enter left-drag / selection state before `GestureDetector.onScroll()` can resolve the pan gesture, and `handlePanEvent` is blocked by `!dragInProgress`.

### Tested versions

Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf]
Related: #82703 (fixed in 4.2 via #82712) — appears to be a regression or an uncovered case of the same face-selection problem.

### System information

macOS 15.7.4 (24G517), Apple Silicon (arm64), Godot v4.7.2.stable.official

### Issue description

On macOS, a `SystemFont` with `font_names = ["PingFang SC"]` resolves to a face that is missing some simplified Chinese glyphs. `Font.has_char()` returns `false` for 迟 (U+8FDF) and 远 (U+8FDC), and these characters render as hex-code placeholder (.notdef) boxes in Labels. Other simplified-only characters (这 边 过 还 进 连 选 设 响 门 关 乐 题 见 页) report `true` and render correctly.

PingFang SC itself definitely contains these characters — it is the macOS Simplified Chinese UI font and renders the same strings correctly in native apps. The pattern (a few simplified-only glyphs missing while most work) suggests the resolver picked a non-SC face from the PingFang font collection — the same class of issue as #82703.

Additional data points:
- Localized family name "苹方-简" shows the same holes.
- PostScript name "PingFangSC-Regular" and weight-qualified names ("PingFang SC Semibold", "PingFang SC Medium") do not resolve at all — `has_char` is false for every tested character.
- Other macOS CJK families resolve with full coverage, including at `font_weight = 600`: Hiragino Sans GB, STHeiti, Heiti SC, Songti SC.
- The `font_names` fallback chain does NOT fill the hole: `["PingFang SC", "Hiragino Sans GB"]` still reports `has_char(迟) == false`. If per-glyph fallback across `font_names` entries is not intended behavior, it may be worth documenting; if it is intended, this is a second bug.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Save the script below as `probe.gd` and run `godot --headless -s probe.gd` in any project.
   (Equivalently, put "延迟设置" into a Label using a SystemFont with "PingFang SC" — 迟 renders as a hex placeholder box.)

func _process(_delta: float) -> bool:
	var f := SystemFont.new()
	f.font_names = PackedStringArray(["PingFang SC"])
	for ch in ["迟", "远", "这", "边", "设", "响"]:
		print(ch, " U+%04X" % ch.unicode_at(0), " has_char=", f.has_char(ch.unicode_at(0)))
	quit()
	return true
```

边 U+8FB9 has_char=true
